findings.F1: A coin's next-day return after a large one-day fall, measured against its prior 20-day volatility, is clearly above normal. In the bottom two of twenty groups the next-day excess return is +0.50 % (t 2.25, n 755) and +0.61 % (t 3.19, n 754). Across all bars the Spearman correlation between the scaled one-day return and the next day's excess return is −0.078 (p 1e-21, n 15076).
findings.F2: The reversal is graded inside the bottom 10 % of scaled one-day returns: the slope of next-day excess return on the scaled return is −0.00463 (t −3.59, n 1509), so the deeper the fall, the larger the rebound.
findings.F3: The rebound after the bottom 10 % of scaled falls holds in both 20-day regimes, at +0.57 % after a 20-day fall (t 3.02, n 1025) and +0.52 % after a 20-day rise (t 2.38, n 484). It is positive in 0.75 of the 24 windows and in all six coins, from +0.26 % for BTC (t 0.95) to +1.02 % for XMR (t 2.92).
findings.F4: The rebound is uneven over the years: +0.82 % in 2018 (t 1.93), +1.52 % in 2020 (t 2.89) and +1.81 % in 2021 (t 3.34), but about zero in 2019, 2022, 2024 and 2025 (from −0.06 % to +0.06 %). Its per-case size, about 0.5–0.6 %, is roughly three times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F5: The idea that was tested depends heavily on the year. Its 10-day excess return in a 20-day rise was +5.30 % in 2020 (t 3.74) and +7.90 % in 2021 (t 3.31), but −10.40 % in 2018 (t −4.19) and −2.60 % in 2023 (t −3.46). That uneven record is consistent with the book's failed Calmar (0.575).
findings.F6: Other angles did not stand out once the number of angles tried is counted. A close near its 30-day high gave +3.07 % over 10 days in the top group (t 2.51, n 282), but the Spearman correlation across all cases was only 0.044 (p 0.10). Weekday effects on the coins' daily returns (Saturday +0.45 %, t 5.5, n 2484) are pooled across correlated coins, so that t is inflated, and Saturday was positive in only 5 of 8 years.
findings.F7: Trades entered on the lowest forecast quartile earned a mean of 17.35 % net, against 6.2–7.2 % for the other quartiles. Those trades lasted 28.4 days against 14–21 days, so holding time carries the trade results more than forecast strength does.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall relative to its typical daily move over the past 20 days, the higher that coin's return over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader can buy a coin at the close of an unusually sharp down day, more the sharper the fall, and expect a rebound of several times the cost of a trade the next day.
ideas.name: sharp falls rebound next day
